newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sembawang questions DBS report on merger.
newsitem.headline: Sembawang questions DBS report on merger.

text.p: Sembawang Corp (SembCorp) has challenged a DBS Securities' analysis report of its proposed merger with Jurong Shipyard.

In a letter to DBS, a copy of which was faxed to Reuters, SembCorp chief financial officer Chan Wing Leong said the company was "puzzled" as to how DBS had arrived at the appraised net tangible asset (NTA) value of Jurong at Singapore $8.95 a share.
SembCorp proposed a merger with Jurong in November in which it would inject S$279.28 million worth of assets into Jurong in exchange for 41.07 million new Jurong shares.
The new Jurong shares were valued at S$6.80 each by SembCorp.
DBS said in its report, which was carried in local newspapers, that the proposed issue price of the new Jurong shares was at a discount to its appraised NTA of S$8.95.
Chan said "retail investors who may be unsophisticated and do not have access to other brokers's reports may regard your appraised NTA value of S$8.95 as a matter of fact".
Chan added he would like DBS to give a more detailed analysis as to how it arrive at the NTA for Jurong, giving the basis and assumptions for the benefit of investors and the press.
